intent_en: To demonstrate that telephone survey results for partisan identification are consistent with those from established federal surveys like the General Social Survey.
previous_intent: To demonstrate that Pew Research Center's telephone surveys produce results similar to the General Social Survey regarding the share of Americans identifying with major political parties from 1990 to 2016.
narration_support: found our polls get very similar numbers on issues like what share of Americans identify as Republicans versus Democrats
chart_support: Two line charts showing the percentage of respondents identifying with the Democratic and Republican parties from 1990 to 2016 for Pew Research Center and the General Social Survey, with the lines tracking closely together
evidence_note: The narration explicitly mentions benchmarking telephone surveys against federal surveys and finding similar numbers on party identification. The chart visually confirms this by plotting Pew Research Center data against General Social Survey data for both Democratic and Republican identification over time, showing high correlation.
